Having received treatment for anorexia, there definitely is some HAES indoctrination going on. I think part of the problem is that when you are underweight from a restrictive ED like anorexia and sometimes bulimia/OSFED and have been restricting a long time, you need a LOT of calories to put on weight. There is a hyper-metabolism response early in the re-feeding phase that continues for 3-6 months after reaching the target weight. I was told to count Starbursts and gummy bears as servings of fruit and was never allowed to pick the sugar-free or "light" versions of foods. And weight gain is crucial for recovery, the obsessive thoughts/anxiety/depression significantly lessens once you've reached a stable weight. I think the problem is that not a lot of ED patients get adequate long-term outpatient coverage so they don't learn how to scale back on their weight-gain diet to a maintenance diet without falling into overt-restriction again and falling through that revolving door of relapse-recovery-relapse. Trying a new diet or exercise routine for someone with an ED is like a recovering alcoholic with a few months of sobriety trying a couple drinks to see if they can handle it. So a lot of people think they have to continue to eat that way to prevent relapse. Then they're all skinny fat but instead of admitting that their treatment providers tell them HAES and body-positivity fluff. It's complicated because a hyper-focus on fitness & nutrition is not helpful in ED recovery either. Treatment centers need to admit we don't really know how to treat anorexia and bulimia and how to get sufferers maintain a healthy relationship with food and their body.
